question: Is the section labeled focus long or dense enough that a reader must track many distinct steps, and do cohesive visible blocks exist that could each stand as a separately named function? Length alone is not enough; name the blocks in your reasoning.

criteria.split_candidate: Cohesive, separately nameable blocks are visible and their interleaving makes the function hard to follow.
criteria.cohesive: The function is short or its steps are already one coherent unit.
criteria.insufficient: The full body is not visible or is too opaque to judge.

evidence.corpus: daily-tracker (sanitized development snapshot, one TypeScript/React Native app)
evidence.sample: top-5 cells by P at or above the 0.7 cut, plus 3 random cells below it
evidence.reviewer: LLM (Claude Opus 5.5), pass 2 with repository access; pass 1 counts in EVIDENCE.md
evidence.note: Reviewed by one LLM reviewer (Claude Opus 5.5) in two passes; not human truth. Cells were the highest-P above the 0.7 cut, so the rate is an upper bound.
